study type: Population-based cohort study with family fixed-effect analysis
exposure: Mode of delivery (caesarean section vs. vaginal birth)
outcome: National Certificate of Educational Achievement (NCEA) percentile scores
cohort: A whole-population cohort of 111,843 children born in New Zealand between January 1, 1996, and December 31, 1998.
finding: Caesarean section was not significantly related to adolescent educational outcomes, particularly after accounting for shared family confounding factors.
mod_finding: After adjustment for confounders, there was no significant association between mode of delivery and university entrance; NCEA percentile scores were initially lower in caesarean-born infants, but this association disappeared in the fixed-effect sibling analysis.
followup_time: Approximately 16-18 years (until secondary school qualification in adolescence)
